_comment_namespace: FIRST FILE IN THE n400 NAMESPACE, AND IT CARRIES REAL CONTENT.
N-400's standing rule (their BACKEND-CONTRACTS.md) is that GP must never
create empty placeholder files for their bespoke names, because a
placeholder turns a loud 404 into a silent versioned {} their decoder
would treat as a real answer. `policy-matrix` is bespoke (it collides
with no flat name), so before this file it 404'd, which was correct.
This file is the answer, not a placeholder. Do not add siblings here
until they hold real content too.

_comment: Scott owns the formal legal review (2026-09-01) and every row below
is an ENGINEERING DEFAULT until he replaces this block with a real
reviewer and date. `basis` on each rule says what the default was
grounded in: PUBLISHED means a citable public source, NEEDS_LEGAL
means the row is a judgment call held at its safest defensible
setting until reviewed. Nothing here reads as reviewed by accident:
tests/test_n400_policy.py fails if status flips to REVIEWED while
any NEEDS_LEGAL row is still ALLOW.

capabilities.basis_note: Rendering speech to text is mechanical and carries no legal conclusion. Transcription happens on device; GP only ever receives text.

Language access is not legal advice. NOTE FOR N-400: the RESTRICT case you described (a locale we do not serve) cannot be expressed on this matrix, because the axes are State x Form and the constraint is per LOCALE. See the ask relayed 2026-09-01.
Reformatting an answer the applicant already gave (a spoken date into YYYY-MM-DD) changes form, not substance.

Writing down what the applicant states is scrivener assistance. USCIS Form N-400 instructions provide for a preparer who fills the form at the applicant's direction, and the form itself carries a preparer certification for exactly that role. TX is the launch jurisdiction; every other state is RESTRICT until reviewed, matching the client's state picker.

Reading back what USCIS itself publishes about a question, in plainer words, states a public source rather than applying it to the applicant's facts. USCIS publishes the N-400 instructions and the Policy Manual openly.

THE LINE ITEM MOST WORTH SCOTT'S REVIEWER'S TIME. Suggesting what an applicant should put on a federal form applies law to their facts, which is the classic boundary of unauthorized practice. Held at ESCALATE rather than BLOCK so the applicant is routed to counsel instead of hitting a wall, but a reviewer may well say BLOCK. Do not relax to ALLOW without a written opinion.

8 CFR 292.1 lists who may represent someone before USCIS: attorneys and DOJ-accredited representatives. This product is neither, and USCIS publishes that same warning to applicants directly (uscis.gov/avoid-scams). Fail closed everywhere.
Naturalization eligibility is USCIS's determination to make, and advising on it is representation under 8 CFR 292.1. BLOCK everywhere, including TX.

ROWS PINNED BY N-400's OWN FIXTURE (Sources/Resources/MockFixtures/policy_matrix.json). Kept byte-identical on purpose so the served matrix and their decode tests cannot disagree. Good moral character is a statutory judgment under INA 316; the client's job here is to stop and refer, never to weigh.

Handing someone to a licensed attorney is the one capability that is always safe, and USCIS publishes the referral surface we point at (uscis.gov/legal-help). ALLOW everywhere so a fail-closed BLOCK elsewhere always has somewhere to send the applicant.
